chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: concerning

A slave marries a free woman, then he is emancipated and afterward commits an indecency. He said, so he said: “There is no rajm upon him until he has intercourse with the free woman after he has been emancipated.”
I said: “Does the free woman have a choice regarding him when he is emancipated?” He said: “No. She was content with him while he was owned, so he remains upon his first marriage.”

key_terms.الْحُرَّةَ: the free woman; his wife in this case
key_terms.الْعَبْدِ: the slave; the male bondman discussed in the ruling
key_terms.رَجْمَ: stoning; the hadd punishment under specified legal conditions
key_terms.فَاحِشَةً: an indecency; here referring to zina
key_terms.مَمْلُوكٌ: owned; still in a state of slavery
key_terms.نِكَاحِهِ: his marriage contract; the existing marital bond
key_terms.يُعْتَقُ: he is emancipated; he becomes free from slavery

ai.seo_question: Does an emancipated slave married to a free woman become subject to rajm, and does his wife gain the option to leave the marriage?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about an emancipated slave who was married to a free woman and then committed zina. It states that rajm does not apply to him unless he has consummated the marriage with the free woman after emancipation, and it also rules that the wife does not gain an option to annul the marriage merely because he was emancipated.
